name: Shrike drill: a SEAD pair with Shrike-class missiles, which a radar beats by going silent
description: The HARM drill's raid with the older missile: two defence-suppression aircraft each with one Shrike-class anti-radiation missile (no memory: when the radar it homes on goes silent it loses lock and falls ballistic), then two strike aircraft. The crew is warned of ARMs and fights with the least emission; the senior operator watches for the signs of a launch and the commander has every transmitter off once the missile in the air has burst. Going silent beats a Shrike even late; against a HARM it has to be early.
notes: The drill: voenizdat_osa_1991 pp262-264 (signs of possible use and of a launch, the least emission, Table 7.3), p238 (a change of position only on the regiment commander's order), p244 (the ARM launch lines on the battery commander's map). The raid is placeholder: routes, heights, speeds, launch ranges and the reserve position are generic numbers. The missiles are the EM library's agm45_class_shrike (data/em/nato_1985.json, estimates as marked there).

relocate_after_arm.notes: The reserve position (placeholder), about 900 m away: some 6 minutes across country at 10 km/h.

arms.notes: Pre-briefed: its intelligence has the battery's position. Fired closer than the HARM (the Shrike's narrow, fixed seeker).
